name: Hoglah
title: One of Zelophehad's Daughters
summary: Hoglah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad from the tribe of Manasseh. She and her sisters are known for claiming their deceased father's inheritance, as he had no sons. Their case led to an important law change in Israel that granted daughters the right to inherit when there were no male heirs.

keyEvents.title: Zelophehad's Daughters Present Their Case Before Moses
keyEvents.description: Hoglah and her four sisters stepped forward before Moses, the priest Eleazar, the tribal leaders, and the entire congregation at the entrance of the Tabernacle to claim their father's inheritance, since he had died without sons.

keyEvents.title: The Lord Upholds the Daughters' Claim
keyEvents.description: God answered Moses and confirmed that Zelophehad's daughters were right, commanding that their father's inheritance be transferred to them. This became a new law in Israel.

keyEvents.title: A New Inheritance Law in Israel
keyEvents.description: Based on the case of Zelophehad's daughters, the Lord established a general rule: If a man dies without sons, his inheritance shall pass to his daughters.

keyEvents.title: Regulation Regarding Marriage Within the Tribe
keyEvents.description: The leaders of the tribe of Manasseh raised concerns that the inheritance might pass to other tribes through marriage. The Lord therefore commanded that Zelophehad's daughters must marry within their own tribe to preserve the inheritance.

keyEvents.title: The Daughters Marry Within the Tribe of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: Hoglah and her sisters obeyed the Lord's command and married men from the tribe of Manasseh, so that their inheritance remained within the tribe.

keyEvents.title: Distribution of the Inheritance in Canaan
keyEvents.description: When Joshua distributed the land of Canaan, Hoglah and her sisters received their father's share in the territory of the tribe of Manasseh, in accordance with the Lord's command through Moses.
